title: kith-jmap: method dispatch registry
description:
Method dispatch table: map JMAP method names to roles, enforce access control, and call handlers.

What: Implement the dispatcher that iterates methodCalls, checks the caller's Role, and either calls the registered handler or returns an error Invocation.

Algorithm:
1. Define const METHOD_ROLES: &[(&str, Role)] listing every known method name and its required role:
   - ('Contact/get', Role::Owner), ('Contact/set', Role::Owner), ('Contact/changes', Role::Owner), ('Contact/query', Role::Owner)
   - ('Chat/get', Role::Owner), ('Chat/set', Role::Owner), ('Chat/changes', Role::Owner), ('Chat/query', Role::Owner)
   - ('Message/get', Role::Owner), ('Message/set', Role::Owner), ('Message/changes', Role::Owner), ('Message/query', Role::Owner), ('Message/queryChanges', Role::Owner)
   - ('Peer/deliver', Role::Peer), ('Peer/receipt', Role::Peer)
2. Define pub trait JmapHandler: Send + Sync { async fn call(&self, caller: &Caller, args: serde_json::Value, store: &Store) -> Result<serde_json::Value, JmapError> }
3. Define pub struct Dispatcher { handlers: HashMap<String, Box<dyn JmapHandler>> }
4. impl Dispatcher { pub fn register(&mut self, method: &str, handler: Box<dyn JmapHandler>) }
5. impl Dispatcher { pub async fn dispatch(&self, request: JmapRequest, caller: &Caller, store: &Store, session_state: String) -> JmapResponse }
   a. For each invocation (name, args, call_id) in request.method_calls:
      - Look up name in METHOD_ROLES; if not found → error invocation (name, unknownMethod, call_id)
      - Check caller.role matches required role; if not → error invocation (name, forbiddenMethod, call_id)
      - Look up handler in self.handlers; if not registered → error invocation (name, unknownMethod, call_id)
      - Call handler.call(caller, args, store); on Err → error invocation; on Ok → success invocation
   b. Return JmapResponse { method_responses: collected invocations, session_state }

Defensive programming rules:
- Role check MUST happen before handler lookup and call (never call handler with wrong role)
- No unwrap() in dispatch loop — every failure returns typed error invocation
- Handler panics must not propagate (catch via Result; wrap in serverFail if needed)
- Unknown method returns unknownMethod, not a 500
- No key material in log statements

Tests:
- Owner calls owner method → dispatched to handler
- Peer calls peer method → dispatched to handler
- Owner calls peer method → error invocation with forbiddenMethod
- Peer calls owner method → error invocation with forbiddenMethod
- Unknown method name → error invocation with unknownMethod
- Mixed batch (some ok, some not) → correct per-invocation results
Oracle: Per-method expected errors constructed manually from RFC 8620 §7.1 error type strings, not derived from dispatch code.
